questions.question: What is the general trend described by Moore's Law in the context of integrated circuits?
options: The number of transistors on an integrated circuit doubles approximately every two years.
The cost of manufacturing chips decreases exponentially every decade.
The speed of processors doubles every 18 months.
The power consumption of chips halves with each new process node.
The physical size of a silicon wafer doubles annually.

questions.question: In the digital IC design flow, after the Register Transfer Level (RTL) design is completed, what is the primary objective of the 'synthesis' step?
options: To verify the functional correctness of the RTL code using simulation.
To generate a physical layout (mask patterns) for manufacturing the chip.
To convert the RTL description into a gate-level netlist using a standard cell library.
To perform static timing analysis on the designed circuit.
To create a comprehensive testbench for design verification.

questions.question: In the context of memory hierarchies in computer architecture, which of the following best describes the principle of 'cache coherence'?
options: Ensuring that multiple processors or cores have access to the same physical main memory addresses.
The mechanism by which data is moved between different levels of the cache hierarchy (e.g., L1 to L2).
Maintaining a consistent view of shared data across multiple caches in a multiprocessor system.
The policy used to decide which data block to evict from the cache when a new block needs to be loaded.
Optimizing the cache line size for improved performance in specific applications.

questions.question: For an out-of-order execution processor, which component is primarily responsible for tracking the state of in-flight instructions, managing their commitment (writing results to architectural state) in program order, and handling precise exceptions?
options: The Reservation Station
The Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB)
The Reorder Buffer (ROB)
The Branch Target Buffer (BTB)
The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)

questions.question: In the manufacturing process of integrated circuits, what is the primary purpose of 'photolithography'?
options: To chemically etch away unwanted material from the silicon wafer.
To deposit thin films of various materials (e.g., metals, dielectrics) onto the wafer surface.
To accurately transfer circuit patterns from a photomask onto the silicon wafer using light-sensitive resist.
To dope specific regions of the silicon with impurities (e.g., boron, phosphorus) to create transistors.
To test the electrical functionality of individual dies on the wafer before packaging.
